lines.text: Some rivalries aren't decided on grass. They are haunted. And no two nations drag more ghosts onto a football pitch than Argentina and England.
Nineteen eighty-six. Maradona beat England twice in four minutes — the Hand of God, then the greatest goal the World Cup had ever seen.
Welcome back to WorldCup twenty-six Legends. Argentina, versus England — a World Cup semifinal, with forty years of ghosts standing on the touchline.
Two of the greatest teams alive walk into the fire. One will reach the final. The other goes home with the ghosts.
Argentina. The world champions. Blue and white, and a number ten who still bends time itself.
Lionel Messi. The captain, number ten. The heir to Maradona, chasing the one crown his country still dreams of.
And Lautaro Martínez, number twenty-two — the bull, always alive in the box.
England. In white, and finally without fear — a golden generation carrying half a century of hurt.
Harry Kane, the captain, number nine. England's greatest ever goalscorer, still hunting his first great trophy.
And Jude Bellingham, number ten — the young king, born for nights exactly like this one.
Because one ghost towers over them all. Nineteen eighty-six — Diego Maradona dragged this same England to its knees, almost alone.
Forty years on, another number ten carries Argentina's dream — and the old man's spirit is watching from the shadows.
This is a semifinal that refuses to breathe. Two giants, trading blow for blow.
England strike first. Anthony Gordon cuts inside and fires them ahead — one, nil.
But Argentina won't go quietly — wave after wave of blue and white, hunting a way back.
The clock becomes the enemy. Eighty minutes gone, still chasing the equalizer.
Then Messi drops a shoulder, rolls it square — Enzo Fernández, twenty yards out.
A thunderbolt. Top corner — eighty-five minutes — one, all! Enzo lit the fuse, but the maestro made it.
Stoppage time. Ninety minutes and two. One last Argentine breath — and it falls to their captain.
Messi glides to the byline and floats it in — and Lautaro Martínez rises above them all. A header. Buried.
Ninety plus two — Argentina two, England one! The bench empties, and forty years of ghosts roar with them.
There is no shootout tonight — no twelve yards of torture. Only Argentina, marching on.
Two goals conjured from nothing. Two assists — both his.
Lionel Messi did not score tonight. He did something rarer — he decided it.
And as the stadium shakes, the boy from Rosario lifts his eyes to the sky — to Diego.
Forty years ago, Maradona beat England alone. Tonight his heir did it as a maestro.
He gives the night to Diego — and Argentina march on, to the final, to face Spain.
No trophy tonight, but something purer — a nation carried, one more time, by its number ten.
The ghost of eighty-six, blessing his heir. The old king and the new, together at last — Argentina, into the final.
The result, in full. Argentina two, England one. Gordon for England; Enzo, then Lautaro deep in stoppage time, for Argentina — with Messi the maker of both.
So you tell me — was this Messi's masterpiece, or England's heartbreak? Comment ARGENTINA, or comment ENGLAND.
And tonight's legend needs no introduction. The ghost that started it all — the immortal number ten.
El Diez. The Hand of God, the Goal of the Century — Diego, whose spirit still carries this Albiceleste.
Legend one-zero-five. El Diez — because some spirits never leave the pitch.
